daily.title: Turn a pasted email chain into actions
daily.task: A long internal email chain about a servicing query lands with you, and you need the open actions and owners.
daily.prompt: You are a mortgage servicing analyst. Below is an anonymised internal email thread I have pasted. List: 1) the issue in two sentences, 2) open actions with owner and due date, 3) unanswered questions. Use a table for actions. Quote the line each action comes from and flag anything unclear. Thread: [paste anonymised thread]
daily.output: A short issue summary, an actions table with owners and dates, and open questions.
daily.check: Each action traces to a quoted line; no customer details slipped into the paste.

daily.title: Draft a clear shift handover note
daily.task: At the end of a shift you have rough jottings and need a tidy handover the next shift can act on.
daily.prompt: Act as a shift handover lead in a mortgage operations team. Turn my rough notes into a handover with headings: Completed, In progress (with next step), Blocked (with reason), Watch-outs. Keep each bullet under 20 words, plain English. Do not add anything not in my notes; mark gaps as [CONFIRM]. Notes: [paste rough notes, no customer data]
daily.output: A structured handover note with four headings and [CONFIRM] markers for gaps.
daily.check: Nothing invented, blocked items are accurate, and [CONFIRM] gaps are resolved.

daily.title: Write an Excel formula to age exceptions
daily.task: Your exceptions log has open dates and statuses, and you need ageing bands to prioritise the backlog.
daily.prompt: I work in Excel with an exceptions log. Column B is Date Raised, column E is Status (Open/Closed). Write a formula for column F that returns ageing bands: 0-2 days, 3-5 days, 6-10 days, over 10 days, using TODAY(), and blank if Closed. Explain each part in plain English and list edge cases to test. Headings only, no data shared.
daily.output: A working ageing-band formula, a plain-English explanation and edge cases to test.
daily.check: Test on a few mock rows, including blanks and weekend dates, before using live.

daily.title: Build a step checklist from an SOP
daily.task: A procedure document is long and dense, and you want a quick checklist to follow while processing cases.
daily.prompt: You are helping a mortgage servicing analyst. From the attached procedure document, create a numbered checklist of every step in order. For each step add the control or check required. Use the document's wording for controls and quote the section number. List any steps that look ambiguous or missing. Do not add steps not in the document. [upload approved SOP]
daily.output: A numbered checklist with controls, section references and a list of ambiguities.
daily.check: Compare against the SOP; the SOP stays the authority, not the checklist.

daily.title: Draft FAQs from a new HR policy
daily.task: A policy has been updated and colleagues will ask the same questions, so you need a clear FAQ.
daily.prompt: You are an HR generalist. From the attached policy, draft 10 FAQs colleagues are likely to ask, with answers in plain UK English under 60 words each. Quote the policy clause each answer relies on. Where the policy is silent, write 'Not covered: ask HR' rather than guessing. [upload approved policy document]
daily.output: Ten plain-English FAQs with clause references and clearly marked gaps.
daily.check: Every answer matches its quoted clause; HR policy owner approves before publishing.

daily.title: Rewrite a job description for clarity
daily.task: A hiring manager's job description is long, jargon-heavy and may put off good candidates.
daily.prompt: You are a talent acquisition partner. Rewrite the job description below in plain, inclusive UK English. Structure: About the role, What you will do (6 bullets), What you bring (essential vs desirable), What we offer. Flag any wording that may be exclusionary or any requirement that seems unnecessary. Keep facts unchanged. JD: [paste draft job description]
daily.output: A restructured, inclusive job description plus flagged wording to discuss.
daily.check: Hiring manager confirms requirements; no facts, grades or benefits changed.

daily.title: Clean a messy joiners list in Excel
daily.task: A joiners list arrives with inconsistent dates, duplicate rows and mixed-case department names before onboarding.
daily.prompt: I have a mock joiners list in Excel: columns Name ID, Start Date (mixed formats), Department (inconsistent case and spelling). Give me step-by-step Excel instructions and formulas to standardise dates to DD/MM/YYYY, fix department names with PROPER and TRIM, and highlight duplicates. Explain each step briefly.
daily.output: Step-by-step cleaning instructions with formulas for dates, text and duplicates.
daily.check: Spot-check cleaned rows against the original; keep an untouched copy.

daily.title: Draft a reply to a policy query
daily.task: A colleague emails asking how a leave policy applies to them, and you need a warm, accurate reply.
daily.prompt: You are an HR generalist. Draft a reply to the anonymised query below using only the attached policy. Tone: warm, clear, professional UK English, under 150 words. Quote the relevant clause. If the answer depends on personal circumstances, say what HR needs to confirm. Query: [paste anonymised query] [upload approved policy]
daily.output: A short, warm draft reply citing the policy clause and any follow-up needed.
daily.check: Clause is correct and current; you decide what is sent and personalise it.

daily.title: Turn a policy into quiz questions
daily.task: You need a short knowledge check after a training module based on an approved policy document.
daily.prompt: You are an L&D specialist. From the attached document, write 8 multiple-choice questions testing understanding, not recall. Each has four options, one correct answer, a one-line explanation and the section it comes from. Mix easy and harder questions. Avoid trick wording. Present as a table. [upload approved training document]
daily.output: Eight multiple-choice questions with answers, explanations and source sections.
daily.check: Subject matter expert confirms answers; no ambiguous or misleading options.

daily.title: Summarise course feedback comments into themes
daily.task: After a session you have dozens of anonymised free-text feedback comments and need the key themes.
daily.prompt: You are a learning coordinator. Group the anonymised feedback comments below into up to six themes. For each theme give a one-line description, count of comments, and two representative quotes. Then list three suggested improvements. Do not infer anything about individuals. Comments: [paste anonymised comments]
daily.output: Up to six themes with counts, sample quotes and suggested improvements.
daily.check: Recount a theme or two by hand; quotes are verbatim.

daily.title: Choose a chart for training completion
daily.task: You have completion data by team and month and need the right visual for a monthly update.
daily.prompt: I have Excel data with columns Team, Month, Enrolled, Completed. I want to show completion progress by team over three months for a leadership update. Suggest the best chart type and one alternative, explain why, and give step-by-step instructions to build it with a PivotTable. Note any misleading design to avoid. Headings only, no data shared.
daily.output: A recommended chart, an alternative, build steps and design pitfalls to avoid.
daily.check: Chart totals reconcile to the source data; axes start sensibly.

daily.title: Draft a session plan from rough ideas
daily.task: You have a topic and rough ideas for a one-hour workshop and need a structured session plan.
daily.prompt: You are an L&D specialist. Turn my notes into a 60-minute session plan as a table: time, activity, purpose, facilitator notes, materials. Include an opener, two practice activities and a recap. Keep it interactive and suitable for a hybrid audience. Notes: [paste topic, audience, learning objectives and rough ideas]
daily.output: A timed session plan table with activities, purpose and facilitator notes.
daily.check: Timings add up to 60 minutes and activities meet the stated objectives.

daily.title: Compare two versions of a policy
daily.task: A risk policy has a new draft and you need to see exactly what changed before review.
daily.prompt: You are a risk analyst. Compare the two attached versions of the policy. Produce a table: section, what changed, old wording (quoted), new wording (quoted), likely impact. Then list changes that may need control updates. Only report differences you can quote; flag anything you are unsure of. [upload version A] [upload version B]
daily.output: A change table with quoted old and new wording and impact notes.
daily.check: Verify each change against both documents; no missed sections.

daily.title: Structure a rough incident write-up
daily.task: You have rough notes on an operational incident and need a clear, consistent write-up for review.
daily.prompt: You are an operational risk analyst. Structure my anonymised notes into an incident summary with headings: What happened, When identified, Impact (as stated), Immediate actions, Root cause (if known), Open questions. Do not assess severity or assign blame; mark gaps as [CONFIRM]. Notes: [paste anonymised incident notes]
daily.output: A structured incident summary with gaps marked for confirmation.
daily.check: Facts match the notes; severity and root cause are decided by people.

daily.title: Build a pivot to track risk actions
daily.task: Your risk action log is a long list and you need overdue actions by owner and rating.
daily.prompt: I have an Excel risk action log with columns Action ID, Owner Team, Rating (High/Medium/Low), Due Date, Status. Explain how to add an Overdue flag with a formula, then build a PivotTable showing overdue counts by Owner Team and Rating. Suggest conditional formatting to highlight High overdue items. Give steps in order. Headings only, no data shared.
daily.output: An overdue formula, PivotTable steps and conditional formatting suggestions.
daily.check: Pivot totals match a manual filter count on the source list.

daily.title: Prepare questions for a control walkthrough
daily.task: You have a process description and need sharp questions before a control walkthrough meeting.
daily.prompt: You are a risk analyst preparing for a control walkthrough. From the attached process description, list: key risks implied by each step, the control that appears to address it, and two questions to ask the process owner. Present as a table. Quote the step text and flag where no control is described. [upload approved process document]
daily.output: A risk-control-question table with gaps flagged for discussion.
daily.check: Risks are plausible for the process; your judgement sets the agenda.

daily.title: Draft variance commentary from your numbers
daily.task: Month-end numbers are done and you need first-draft commentary explaining the main variances.
daily.prompt: You are a management accountant. Using the variance table and driver notes below, draft commentary for each line with a variance over [threshold]: what moved, why (only from my notes), and whether it is timing or permanent. Under 40 words per line, neutral tone. Mark any line without an explanation as [EXPLANATION NEEDED]. Data: [paste table and notes]
daily.output: Draft commentary per material line, with unexplained variances clearly marked.
daily.check: Figures and reasons match your workings; nothing speculative left in.

daily.title: Explain an inherited Excel formula
daily.task: You inherited a spreadsheet with a long nested formula and need to understand it before relying on it.
daily.prompt: Explain this Excel formula step by step in plain English, as if to a new team member. Then say what inputs it expects, what could make it return a wrong result, and suggest a simpler or more robust version if one exists (for example XLOOKUP or LET). Formula: [paste formula] Context: [describe the columns it references]
daily.output: A plain-English breakdown, risks of error and a possible simpler formula.
daily.check: Test the original and any rewrite on the same mock data; results must match.

daily.title: Summarise a regulatory update for your team
daily.task: A published regulatory notice is long and you need a short summary of what it means for reporting.
daily.prompt: You are a regulatory reporting analyst. Summarise the attached published notice: 1) what is changing, 2) effective dates, 3) which reports or data items may be affected, 4) questions to raise with the policy owner. Quote the paragraph for each point. Flag anything you are unsure of; do not interpret beyond the text. [upload published notice]
daily.output: A four-part summary with quoted paragraphs and questions for the policy owner.
daily.check: Dates and scope match the source; compliance interpretation stays with experts.

daily.title: Prepare for a budget review meeting
daily.task: You have a briefing pack for tomorrow's budget review and want the key points and likely questions.
daily.prompt: You are a management accountant preparing for a budget review. From the attached pack, give me: five key messages, the three biggest risks or variances, and eight questions stakeholders are likely to ask, each with the page or table I should point to. Keep it to one page. Flag figures that look inconsistent. [upload briefing pack]
daily.output: A one-page prep sheet with key messages, risks and likely questions.
daily.check: Figures quoted match the pack; inconsistencies are checked, not assumed.

daily.title: Build a document checklist from lending criteria
daily.task: Lending criteria documents are detailed and you want a quick checklist of required documents per case type.
daily.prompt: You are an underwriting support analyst. From the attached approved lending criteria, create a checklist of required documents and checks for [case type, e.g. buy-to-let limited company]. Group by stage. Quote the criteria section for each item. Flag anything ambiguous. Do not make or suggest any lending decision. [upload approved criteria document]
daily.output: A staged document checklist with criteria references and ambiguities flagged.
daily.check: Matches the current criteria version; underwriters make every decision.

daily.title: Draft a clear reply to a broker query
daily.task: A broker has sent a process question by email and you need a clear, accurate, professional reply.
daily.prompt: You are a broker support analyst. Draft a reply to the anonymised broker query below using only the attached approved guidance. Tone: professional, helpful, plain UK English, under 150 words. Quote the guidance section relied on. If the answer needs an underwriter's view, say so rather than answering. Query: [paste anonymised query] [upload approved guidance]
daily.output: A concise draft reply grounded in approved guidance, with referrals noted.
daily.check: Guidance is current; no case-specific promise or decision implied.

daily.title: Summarise the application pipeline with a pivot
daily.task: You have a mock or approved pipeline extract and need cases by stage and age for a weekly update.
daily.prompt: I have an approved Excel pipeline extract with columns Case Ref, Product Type, Stage, Date Received, Broker Channel. Show me how to add a Days in Stage column, then build a PivotTable of case counts by Stage and age band, and suggest one chart for a weekly update. Give numbered steps and formulas. Headings only, no data shared.
daily.output: Formula for days in stage, PivotTable steps and a chart suggestion.
daily.check: Counts reconcile to the extract; extract contains no customer names.

daily.title: Summarise valuation report points for review
daily.task: A long anonymised valuation report needs its key points pulled out for the underwriter's attention.
daily.prompt: You are an underwriting support analyst. From the attached anonymised valuation report, list the key factual points: property type, condition notes, any recommendations, retentions or caveats. Quote the page and line for each. Do not assess suitability or make any recommendation on the case. Flag anything unclear. [upload anonymised valuation report]
daily.output: A factual list of key points with page references for the underwriter.
daily.check: Every point traces to the report; the underwriter forms the view.

daily.title: Rewrite a customer letter in plain English
daily.task: A template letter about an account change is wordy, and Consumer Duty expects clear, understandable communication.
daily.prompt: You are a savings operations analyst. Rewrite the template letter below in plain UK English for a general reader: short sentences, key information first, no jargon, active voice. Keep every fact, date and rate placeholder unchanged. Then list what you simplified and any sentence that may still confuse customers. Letter: [paste template with placeholders]
daily.output: A plain-English letter draft plus a list of changes and remaining risks.
daily.check: Facts unchanged; template goes through the normal approval route.

daily.title: Turn rough meeting notes into actions
daily.task: After a team huddle on a process change, your notes are scattered and you need agreed actions.
daily.prompt: You are a savings operations analyst. Turn my rough meeting notes into: a three-line summary, decisions made, and an actions table (action, owner, due date). Only use what is in the notes; mark missing owners or dates as [TBC]. Keep it ready to paste into a follow-up email. Notes: [paste notes, no customer data]
daily.output: A brief summary, decisions list and actions table with [TBC] gaps.
daily.check: Decisions reflect what was agreed; fill [TBC] items before sharing.

daily.title: Spot gaps in a daily processing tracker
daily.task: Your daily processing tracker has missing values and inconsistent statuses that skew the weekly summary.
daily.prompt: I have an Excel tracker with columns Date, Process Type, Items Received, Items Completed, Status. Give me formulas and steps to: find blank or non-numeric cells, standardise Status values to a fixed list using data validation, and flag rows where Completed exceeds Received. Explain each step briefly. Headings only, no data shared.
daily.output: Formulas and steps to find gaps, standardise statuses and flag anomalies.
daily.check: Check flagged rows by hand; keep the original data unchanged.

daily.title: Draft internal FAQs for a product change
daily.task: An approved product change note has arrived and colleagues need quick internal FAQs to answer questions consistently.
daily.prompt: You are a savings product support analyst. From the attached approved change note, draft 8 internal FAQs colleagues may need, with short plain-English answers. Quote the section each answer uses. Where the note does not answer something, write 'Not covered: check with product owner'. Do not invent rates or dates. [upload approved change note]
daily.output: Eight internal FAQs with source sections and clearly marked gaps.
daily.check: Product owner confirms answers; rates and dates match the note exactly.

daily.title: Draft a walkthrough request list
daily.task: Before fieldwork you need a clear evidence request list based on the audit scope and process documents.
daily.prompt: You are an internal auditor. Using the attached audit scope and process document, draft an evidence request list as a table: request number, item requested, purpose, related control, suggested format. Group by process area. Quote the scope or process line each request supports. Flag areas where scope is unclear. [upload scope] [upload process document]
daily.output: A grouped evidence request table linked to scope and controls.
daily.check: Requests are proportionate and in scope; audit lead approves before sending.

daily.title: Tighten the wording of a draft finding
daily.task: Your draft audit finding is long and loosely worded and needs to be clear, factual and balanced.
daily.prompt: You are an internal auditor. Rewrite my draft finding using the structure: Condition, Criteria, Cause, Consequence, Recommendation. Keep it factual, neutral and concise. Do not change facts, rating or evidence references. Highlight any statement not supported by the evidence I describe. Draft: [paste anonymised draft finding and evidence summary]
daily.output: A restructured finding in the five Cs format, with unsupported statements flagged.
daily.check: Facts and rating unchanged; the auditor owns the conclusion.

daily.title: Select a sample with Excel formulas
daily.task: You need a simple, documented sample from an approved population list for testing.
daily.prompt: I have an approved population list in Excel with columns Item ID, Date, Amount, Team. Explain how to draw a random sample of [n] items using RAND or RANDARRAY, how to fix the values so the sample does not change, and how to add a stratified option by Team. Include steps to document the method for working papers.
daily.output: Sampling steps, formulas and a short method note for working papers.
daily.check: Sample size follows audit methodology; method is reproducible and recorded.

daily.title: Prepare for an audit closing meeting
daily.task: You have the draft report and want to anticipate management's questions before the closing meeting.
daily.prompt: You are an internal auditor preparing for a closing meeting. From the attached draft report, list for each finding: the likely management challenge, the evidence I should have ready, and a calm, factual response point. Present as a table. Do not change ratings or conclusions. [upload anonymised draft report]
daily.output: A table of likely challenges, evidence to have ready and response points.
daily.check: Evidence references exist in working papers; ratings remain the auditor's call.

daily.title: Draft a polite supplier chaser email
daily.task: A supplier has not sent a corrected invoice despite earlier requests, and you need a firm but polite chaser.
daily.prompt: You are an accounts payable analyst. Draft a polite but firm email to a supplier asking for a corrected invoice. Context: [what is wrong, dates of previous requests]. Tone: professional UK English, under 120 words, clear ask and deadline of [date]. Offer two subject line options. Use [Supplier name] and [Invoice ref] placeholders.
daily.output: A short chaser email with a clear ask and two subject lines.
daily.check: Facts and dates are right; you send it from your own mailbox.

daily.title: Match two lists with XLOOKUP
daily.task: You have a ledger extract and a statement extract and need to find unmatched items quickly.
daily.prompt: I have two Excel sheets: Ledger (Ref, Date, Amount) and Statement (Ref, Date, Amount). Write formulas to flag, for each ledger row, whether the Ref exists on the Statement and whether the amount matches, using XLOOKUP. Then explain how to filter unmatched items and summarise them by age. Mention common causes of false mismatches. Headings only, no data shared.
daily.output: Matching formulas, filtering steps and common causes of false mismatches.
daily.check: Test on mock data; investigate breaks yourself before any adjustment.

daily.title: Write clear reconciliation break commentary
daily.task: Month-end reconciliation has open breaks and reviewers need concise, consistent commentary for each.
daily.prompt: You are a reconciliation analyst. Turn my rough notes on each open break into consistent commentary: reference, amount, age, reason (from my notes only), next action, owner. Under 30 words per break. Mark breaks without a known reason as [UNDER INVESTIGATION]. Notes: [paste anonymised break notes]
daily.output: Consistent one-line commentary per break with next actions and owners.
daily.check: Amounts and ages match the reconciliation; reasons are evidenced.

daily.title: Turn a payments procedure into quick reference
daily.task: The invoice processing procedure is long and new joiners need a one-page quick reference.
daily.prompt: You are an accounts payable analyst. From the attached approved procedure, create a one-page quick reference: key steps in order, approval limits as written, common mistakes to avoid, and who to contact (use [team] placeholders). Quote the section for each step. Do not change any limit or control. [upload approved procedure]
daily.output: A one-page quick reference with steps, controls and section references.
daily.check: Limits and controls match the procedure exactly; procedure owner reviews.

daily.title: Compare two supplier proposals side by side
daily.task: Two supplier proposals have arrived in different formats and you need a fair side-by-side comparison.
daily.prompt: You are a procurement analyst. Compare the two attached supplier proposals against these criteria: [list criteria]. Produce a table with each criterion, what each supplier offers (quoted with page), and gaps or unclear points. Do not score or recommend a supplier. List clarification questions for each. [upload proposal A] [upload proposal B]
daily.output: A criteria comparison table with quotes, gaps and clarification questions.
daily.check: Quotes are accurate; evaluation and scoring stay with the panel.

daily.title: Draft clarification questions for a supplier
daily.task: A tender response is vague in places and you need precise clarification questions to send.
daily.prompt: You are a procurement analyst. Review the attached supplier response against our requirements below. List up to 10 precise clarification questions where the response is vague, incomplete or inconsistent. For each, quote the response text and the requirement. Keep questions neutral and specific. Requirements: [paste requirements] [upload supplier response]
daily.output: Up to ten neutral, specific clarification questions with supporting quotes.
daily.check: Questions are fair to all bidders and follow procurement process.

daily.title: Find contracts due for renewal in Excel
daily.task: Your contract register is long and you need to see which contracts expire in the next quarter.
daily.prompt: I have an Excel contract register with columns Supplier, Category, Start Date, End Date, Notice Period (days), Owner. Write formulas to calculate the notice deadline and days remaining, flag contracts needing action within 90 days, and build a PivotTable by Category and Owner. Suggest conditional formatting for urgency. Headings only, no data shared.
daily.output: Deadline formulas, a 90-day flag, PivotTable steps and formatting tips.
daily.check: Verify a few dates against the contracts; register stays the source.

daily.title: Prepare an agenda for a supplier review
daily.task: A quarterly supplier review is coming up and you have performance notes and the contract summary.
daily.prompt: You are a supplier management analyst. From my notes and the attached contract summary, draft a 45-minute supplier review agenda with timings, discussion points, evidence to bring and questions to ask. Highlight any service commitments from the contract that the notes suggest are at risk, quoting the clause. Notes: [paste notes] [upload contract summary]
daily.output: A timed agenda with discussion points, evidence needs and at-risk commitments.
daily.check: Clauses are quoted correctly; performance judgements are yours.

daily.title: Turn a QA framework into a checklist
daily.task: The quality assurance framework is long and you want a practical checklist to use while reviewing cases.
daily.prompt: You are a quality checker. From the attached approved QA framework, build a checklist table: check number, what to check, pass criteria (quoted from the framework), section reference. Group by stage of the process. Flag criteria that seem subjective or unclear. Do not add new criteria. [upload approved QA framework]
daily.output: A grouped checklist with quoted pass criteria and unclear items flagged.
daily.check: Matches the current framework; outcomes remain the checker's judgement.

daily.title: Write constructive feedback on a reviewed case
daily.task: You have reviewed a case and need clear, constructive feedback for the colleague who processed it.
daily.prompt: You are a quality checker. Turn my review notes into constructive feedback: what went well, what needs correcting (with the framework reference), and one practical tip. Tone: supportive, specific, UK English, under 150 words. Do not change my findings or outcome. Notes: [paste anonymised review notes]
daily.output: Supportive, specific feedback with framework references and a practical tip.
daily.check: Findings and outcome unchanged; tone suits the colleague and context.

daily.title: Find recurring errors with a pivot
daily.task: Your QA results log is growing and you want to see which error types recur by process.
daily.prompt: I have an Excel QA log with columns Review Date, Process, Error Category, Severity, Outcome. Explain how to build a PivotTable showing error counts by Process and Error Category, filtered by month, and how to rank the top five categories. Suggest a chart to show trends over three months. Give numbered steps. Headings only, no data shared.
daily.output: PivotTable and ranking steps plus a trend chart suggestion.
daily.check: Totals match the log; categories are used consistently before analysis.

daily.title: Proofread a template for clarity and errors
daily.task: A customer-facing template needs a final proofread for errors, clarity and consistency before approval.
daily.prompt: You are a quality analyst. Proofread the template below. Return a table: original text, issue (spelling, grammar, clarity, consistency, jargon), suggested fix. Use UK English. Do not change meaning, figures or placeholders. Finally, rate overall readability for a general customer and explain briefly. Template: [paste template with placeholders]
daily.output: A table of issues with suggested fixes and a readability note.
daily.check: Meaning and placeholders unchanged; template follows normal approval.

daily.title: Theme anonymised customer feedback comments
daily.task: You have a batch of anonymised survey comments and need themes to support a monthly insight pack.
daily.prompt: You are an insights analyst. Group the anonymised survey comments below into up to eight themes. For each: theme name, short description, number of comments, sentiment (positive, neutral, negative) and two verbatim quotes. Note comments that fit no theme. Do not infer anything about individuals. Comments: [paste anonymised comments]
daily.output: Themes with counts, sentiment, verbatim quotes and unthemed comments.
daily.check: Recount a sample of themes; quotes are verbatim and anonymised.

daily.title: Pick the right chart for a question
daily.task: A stakeholder asks a question of your survey data, and you need the clearest chart to answer it.
daily.prompt: I have Excel survey data with columns Month, Channel, Product, Satisfaction Score (1-5), Response Count. The question is: [stakeholder question]. Recommend the best chart and one alternative, explain why, list the PivotTable fields to use, and note any design choices that could mislead. Give build steps.
daily.output: A chart recommendation, PivotTable fields, build steps and pitfalls.
daily.check: Chart answers the actual question; small sample sizes are labelled.

daily.title: Draft a neutral customer survey
daily.task: You need a short survey about a service journey, with questions that are clear and unbiased.
daily.prompt: You are a customer research analyst. Draft a 10-question survey about [journey, e.g. fixed-rate savings maturity]. Mix rating and open questions. Use plain, neutral UK English, avoid leading or double-barrelled questions, and do not ask for personal data. After the draft, list any question that might still bias answers.
daily.output: A ten-question neutral survey plus a list of potential bias risks.
daily.check: Questions match the research objective; survey follows approval process.

daily.title: Turn findings into a one-page summary
daily.task: Your analysis is done and senior stakeholders want a short, clear summary of what it shows.
daily.prompt: You are an insights analyst. Turn my findings below into a one-page summary: headline (one sentence), three key insights with supporting figures from my notes, what it may mean, and suggested next questions. Plain UK English. Do not add figures not in my notes; flag weakly supported points. Findings: [paste aggregated findings]
daily.output: A one-page summary with headline, insights, implications and next questions.
daily.check: Every figure traces to your analysis; caveats are clearly stated.
